question: What is the primary purpose of a medical drainage system?

options.A: To remove unwanted fluids or air from the body
options.B: To prevent the formation of normal scar tissue
options.C: To deliver intravenous medications directly into a wound
options.D: To maintain high intra-abdominal pressure during surgery

explanation: Drainage systems are specifically designed to clear out pathological accumulations like pus, blood, or air to aid healing. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T22#GNS212_U1_T22_h1)

question: Why is accurate monitoring of drainage output clinically vital?

options.A: It helps evaluate the patient's recovery and detect hidden complications
options.B: It guarantees that the patient will not develop a systemic infection
options.C: It replaces the need for standard vital sign measurements
options.D: It dictates the exact schedule for future surgical operations

explanation: Tracking volume and character allows nurses to spot abnormal changes like sudden hemorrhage early. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T22#GNS212_U1_T22_h1)

question: A drain placed to prevent fluid accumulation in a surgical dead space is classified as what type?
explanation: Prophylactic drains are put in place proactively to stop fluid from pooling where a cavity was closed. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T22#GNS212_U1_T22_h2)

question: What clinical scenario represents a therapeutic indication for drainage?

options.A: Anticipating mild swelling after a minor skin biopsy
options.C: Collecting a routine blood sample from a peripheral vein
options.D: Administering a prophylactic dose of intravenous antibiotics

explanation: Therapeutic drains actively treat and remove existing pathological collections like pus or large hematomas. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T22#GNS212_U1_T22_h2)

question: Which characteristic best describes a closed drainage system?

options.A: It connects to a sealed collection container preventing external contact
options.B: It is impossible to measure the total fluid output accurately
options.C: It relies entirely on gravity without any tubing attachments
options.D: It drains freely onto sterile gauze pads kept on the wound surface

explanation: Closed systems maintain a closed circuit from the patient to the reservoir, reducing infection risks. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T22#GNS212_U1_T22_h3)

question: What is the main safety advantage of using a closed drain over an open drain?

options.A: Decreased risk of retrograde microbial entry into the body
options.B: Elimination of the need for any surgical dressings
options.C: Faster spontaneous tissue healing without scarring
options.D: Complete prevention of tube blockages and kinking

explanation: Because the system is sealed, bacteria from the environment have a much harder time traveling back up into the wound. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T22#GNS212_U1_T22_h3)

question: Which drainage tube is specifically placed in the common bile duct after gallbladder surgery?
explanation: A T-tube keeps the common bile duct open and drains bile externally until normal flow into the duodenum resumes. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T22#GNS212_U1_T22_h4)

question: A patient with an intestinal obstruction requires gastric decompression. Which tube is most appropriate?
explanation: An NG tube allows suctioning of gastric secretions and gas, relieving nausea, vomiting, and abdominal distension. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T22#GNS212_U1_T22_h4)

question: What finding around a surgical drain insertion site most strongly suggests a developing infection?

options.A: A small amount of dried blood on the suture line
options.C: Clear serosanguineous fluid on the dressing
options.D: Normal skin coloration surrounding the tubing

explanation: Pus and spreading redness are classic signs of localized bacterial infection around a wound or drain site. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T22#GNS212_U1_T22_h5)

question: A nurse notices that a closed suction drain has stopped producing fluid completely over the last six hours, yet the patient's abdomen is becoming increasingly distended and firm. What is the most likely issue?

options.A: The suction chamber was compressed too tightly
options.B: The body has naturally stopped producing any fluids
options.C: The drain is likely blocked or kinked internally
options.D: The patient has fully healed and no longer needs output

explanation: Abdominal distension alongside sudden zero output suggests fluid is accumulating inside because the drain is obstructed. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T22#GNS212_U1_T22_h5)

question: Why must a bulb-style suction drain be compressed and closed after emptying?

options.A: To prevent the tubing from adhering to internal body tissues
options.B: To prevent air from entering the patient's bloodstream
options.C: To reestablish negative pressure for continuous suction
options.D: To stop the collection chamber from leaking fluid onto the bed

explanation: Compressing the bulb and closing the plug creates the vacuum required to pull fluid out of the surgical site. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T22#GNS212_U1_T22_h6)

question: Which nursing action is essential when securing a patient's drainage tubing to their bed or gown?

options.A: Allowing enough slack for safe patient movement without pulling
options.B: Taping the entire length of the tube to the patient's skin
options.C: Pinning the tubing tightly to ensure it never shifts position
options.D: Placing the collection bag higher than the insertion site

explanation: Providing adequate slack prevents accidental dislodgement when the patient turns or sits up. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T22#GNS212_U1_T22_h6)

question: What is the primary danger of forcing irrigation fluid into a blocked surgical drain without a specific medical order?

options.A: Introducing bacteria and disrupting delicate healing tissues
options.B: Instantly lowering the patient's systemic blood pressure
options.C: Turning serous fluid into bright red arterial blood
options.D: Causing the collection chamber to expand too rapidly

explanation: Unordered or forceful irrigation can force pathogens deep into the wound and damage fragile internal suture lines. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T22#GNS212_U1_T22_h7)

question: What immediate action should a nurse take if a surgical drain falls out completely?

options.A: Leave the open wound completely exposed to dry in the air
options.B: Attempt to reinsert the exact same tubing back into the wound
options.C: Clamp all remaining lines and administer a strong pain reliever
options.D: Cover the site with a sterile dressing and notify the clinician

explanation: A sterile dressing protects the open exit site from contamination while awaiting medical assessment for potential replacement. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T22#GNS212_U1_T22_h7)

question: Which preparation step is most helpful before a nurse removes a painful surgical drain?

options.A: Encouraging the patient to walk rapidly around the ward
options.B: Clamping the tube for twenty-four hours continuously
options.C: Flushing the drainage system with sterile normal saline

explanation: Giving analgesics before removal helps manage the discomfort associated with pulling the device out of the tissue tract. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T22#GNS212_U1_T22_h8)

question: What is the primary reason for applying an occlusive dressing immediately after a drain is pulled out?

options.A: To keep the skin moist so new tissue forms over the opening
options.B: To prevent the patient from touching the healing skin area
options.C: To seal the wound tract and prevent air or fluid leakage
options.D: To increase local body temperature and speed up scar fading

explanation: An occlusive dressing covers the open tract to protect it from outside bacteria and absorb any lingering drainage. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T22#GNS212_U1_T22_h8)
